{{Quote|Okay, you're in Keldabe, on Mandalore. I'm Medrit Vasur. This is my farm, and you can stay here until you're well enough to leave.|[[Medrit Vasur]], speaking with [[Sintas Vel]]|<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>}}
The '''Beviin-Vasur farm''' was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]]-owned [[Farm/Legends|farm]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Located ten [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] outside of the planet's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], the large farm was [[Fortress/Legends|walled]] and possessed a number of outbuildings and traditional Mandalorian ''[[Vheh'yaim/Legends|vheh'yaime'']], all connected by underground tunnels and positioned around the main stone farmhouse.

The farm was owned by [[Goran Beviin]] and his [[Marriage/Legends|husband]], [[Medrit Vasur]], and became the family home of [[Clan Beviin]]. There, Beviin and Vasur lived with their [[Gai bal manda|adopted]] daughter [[Dinua Jeban|Dinua]]; by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], they were also joined by Dinua's own family, including her husband [[Jintar]], and their two children, [[Briila]] and [[Shalk]]. When [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], a friend of Beviin, came to Mandalore in an attempt to become closer to his people and the Mandalorian culture, Fett was allowed to to stay at the farm. Similar arrangements were made when [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] arrived on Mandalore, seeking Fett's aid in defeating her recently turned [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Caedus|brother]].

==Description==
{{Quote|There's always room at the farm.|[[Goran Beviin]]|<ref name="Revelation" />}}
[[File:Vhehyaim-Insider86.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Several traditional ''vheh'yaime'' were set up across the farm.]]
The Beviin-Vasur [[Farm/Legends|farm]] was located on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="Sacrifice" /> a world in the region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] known as the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Situated on land approximately ten [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] from Mandalore's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], the Beviin-Vasur farm was a sprawling collection of traditional Mandalorian ''[[Vheh'yaim/Legends|vheh'yaime'']], camouflaged and sunk into the ground, in addition to numerous other outbuildings that served a variety of purposes. Each of these buildings was linked via a network of underground tunnels, and the tunnels themselves provided an escape off into the hills west of the farm. Dirtworks and a sturdy [[Fortress/Legends|wall emplacement]] around the outside reaches of the Beviin-Vasur farm served as means of defense and protection, and the old stone farmhouse at the center of the scattered other buildings served as both the home of the farm's owners, and the last fallback bastion in the event of an attack. The front entrance to the farmhouse was dug into the ground, and was accessed by a short series of carved steps;<ref name="Sacrifice" /> inside the two-level building was a kitchen, several bedrooms, and a common room<ref name="Revelation" /> Mandalorians referred to as a ''kar'yai''.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

At the rear of the farmhouse, and attached to the main building by one of the many underground tunnels, was a workshop equipped with tools and a forge designed for [[Metalsmith/Legends|metalwork]]. Smoke from the forge's [[Fire/Legends|fire]] was funneled out through a vent into the open air several [[Meter/Legends|meters]] from the shop, in order to help disguise the workshop's location from any unwanted onlookers.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Another feature of the Beviin-Vasur farm was the barn used to house the farm's animals and other equipment, including a [[Harvester droid/Legends|harvester droid]]. Constructed out of sheets of [[Duraplast/Legends|duraplast]] and timber boards, with large double-doors at one end, the barn's assembly left roughly spaced gaps between the outer boards wide enough to allow rays of [[Star/Legends|sunlight]] to enter. An old dirt road stretched between the Beviin-Vasur farm and the [[Levet's farm|farm]] belonging to the Mandalorian [[Levet]].<ref name="Revelation" />

==History==
{{Quote|She's at Beviin's farm.|[[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], speaking about Sintas Vel|<ref name="Revelation" />}}
The home of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Clan Beviin|Beviin clan]], the Beviin-Vasur farm was owned and maintained by the Mandalorian couple [[Goran Beviin]] and [[Medrit Vasur]]. Vasur was worked as a [[Metalsmith/Legends|blacksmith]] from the farm's workshop, where he forged weapons and armor from Mandalorian ''beskar'' iron. Beviin enjoyed working around the farm, even when it came to jobs such as cleaning up animal dung.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> However, Beviin was also occasionally forced to take up part-[[Time/Legends|time]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] work to make ends meet when the farm came upon lean times. One such instance was around [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], when a rough [[Standard year/Legends|year]] had left Beviin and Medrit with no profit income from the farm, and Beviin accepted a job from the mysterious individual known as Udelen—secretly the advanced [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Nom Anor]] in disguise. This opened the door for an unknowing alliance between the Mandalorians and the Yuuzhan Vong until [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], when the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extragalactic]] invaders launched their attack on the known galaxy. During the first year of the resulting [[Yuuzhan Vong War|galactic war]], Beviin's friend [[Briika Jeban]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by a [[Bur'lorr|Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Subaltern]] on [[New Holgha]]. Keeping a promise he had made to her when the Yuuzhan Vong had first made themselves known, Beviin adopted Jeban's daughter [[Dinua Jeban|Dinua]] in the [[Gai bal manda|Mandalorian tradition]].<ref name="APM">''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''</ref> By the war's end, Dinua had come to live at the farm on Mandalore with Beviin and Medrit.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

By the year [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], Dinua had gotten [[Marriage/Legends|married]] to a Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] named [[Jintar]] and had two kids, a son and daughter named [[Shalk]] and [[Briila]], respectively. This second generation of family also resided on the farm along with Beviin and Vasur. As the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] broke out, Jintar left to seek mercenary work in the war, while Beviin offered to allow his friend and reigning [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], to stay at the farm during his time living on Mandalore. Fett accepted, though he took up residence within his parked [[Starship/Legends|ship]], [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']], rather than the farmhouse. When a fresh lode of ''beskar'' iron was found north of the city of [[Enceri]], the Beviin-Vasur farm's workshop became a testing ground for the new metal, as Vasur utilized samples to forge traditional Mandalorian ''[[Beskad/Legends|beskad]]'' [[Sword/Legends|sabers]]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|''beskar'' armor]].<ref name="Revelation" />

When [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] journeyed to Mandalore seeking to learn from Boba Fett new skills to defeat her brother, the recently anointed [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Caedus]], Solo was allowed to stay at the Beviin-Vasur farm for the duration of her time on the planet. The farm's barn was used as a training ground during Solo's initial sparring session with Fett, and she repaid the kindness of the Beviin clan by putting her technical skills to use working on the farm's equipment. Beviin and Vasur's farm was also the temporary home of [[Sintas Vel]], Fett's long-lost ex wife, during her period of recovering from years of [[Carbonite/Legends|carbon freeze]].<ref name="Revelation" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Beviin-Vasur farm was first mentioned in the [[2006]] [[EBook|e-novella]] ''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]'', by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]]. It was mentioned again in Traviss' first entry into the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' novel series, entitled ''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]'', before making its first full appearance in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in Traviss' second ''Legacy of the Force'' title, ''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''. ''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]'', Traviss' third entry to the series, again featured the Beviin-Vasur farm as a prominent locale.
